version.note: Neither recording entry identifies the performing edition. The first edition and revised 1947 text are not interchangeable provenance claims. Listening notes distinguish written cluster techniques from what the recording establishes; no particular board, hand position or edition-specific bar alignment is asserted for Liang.

performers.note: Commons credits Liang for performance and recording; the corresponding IMSLP entry explicitly identifies piano. No additional performer is named. This solo-piano package has no orchestral stage timeline.

date.note: Commons’ Summary gives 2024 for the performance/recording. The file was uploaded on 11 June 2024, earlier than the other three Commons movements; this is an upload date, not a session day. A common session for the sonata is not established.

place.note: No recording venue, city, piano or live-versus-studio setting is identified in the consulted recording entries.

label.note: No record label is identified. IMSLP gives ‘Eric Xi Xin Liang, 2024’ as the audio publisher, not a named commercial label. Neither recording entry links sleeve or label scans.

catalogue.note: No original carrier catalogue number is supplied. IMSLP file index 918634 is a repository identifier, not a record catalogue number.

matrixTakeSides.note: No matrix, take or disc-side identifier is supplied. The digital distribution format alone does not establish the original session medium or take history.

composition.value: Public domain as asserted in Commons’ separate musical-composition notice
composition.note: Commons’ composition notice cites Ives’s death in 1954 and publication before 1931. It does not license the sound recording. Gann distinguishes 1920 printing, January 1921 circulation and the revised 1947 edition. The performing edition is unknown; later revisions or editorial additions are not independently cleared by the first-publication notice. IMSLP marks the revised score non-public-domain in the United States.

Appropriate attribution and a licence link are required; the recording is not claimed to be public domain.

sources.title: Kyle Gann — Following the Concord Sonata, Charles Ives Society
sources.locator: Hawthorne section: opening, quiet clusters, ragtime, Martyn interruptions, march, fist-cluster climax, cumulative Columbia material and closing rapid figuration. Literary interpretations are distinguished from Ives’s own statements. Chronology distinguishes composition and editions.

sources.title: Charles Ives — Essays Before a Sonata
sources.locator: Introduction calls Hawthorne a scherzo; the Hawthorne essay’s final paragraphs distinguish the novelist’s moral subject matter from the fantastic realm attempted by this movement. The modern prefatory biographical sketch is not used as Ives’s testimony.

sources.title: Jan Swafford — Ives The Man: His Life
sources.locator: ‘like father, like son’: the remembered childhood story of playing drum parts with fists on the piano, explicitly reported as Ives’s own account.
